__NOTOC__ Knucklerot is an elite abomination who patrols the areas near the Howling Ziggurat and Bleeding Ziggurat in the Ghostlands. Knucklerot and Luzran were created by Dar'Khan Drathir.

Knight-Lieutenant's Dragonhide Gloves was part of Lieutenant Commander's Sanctuary, the Alliance PvP-Rare set for druids. It can no longer be obtained, having been replaced by Knight-Lieutenant's Dragonhide Grips of the Lieutenant Commander's Refuge set. Players who had earned this item could use it with the newer set's items and still gain the set bonus, prior to the set bonus being made inactive in patch 7.0.3.

Knight-Lieutenant's Chain Boots is mail foot armor for hunters. It is part of the now obsolete Rare-Quality PvP-reward set Lieutenant Commander's Pursuit, and became available to purchase at selected vendors at rank 8. In Patch 1.11 players with rank 8 or higher will be able to purchase the upgraded replacement Pursuance item - the Knight-Lieutenant's Chain Greaves.

Knight-Lieutenant's Chain Gauntlets is mail hand armor for hunters. It is part of the now obsolete Rare-Quality PvP-reward set Lieutenant Commander's Pursuit, and became available to purchase at selected vendors at rank 8. In Patch 1.11 players with rank 8 or higher will be able to purchase the upgraded replacement Pursuance item - the Knight-Lieutenant's Chain Vices.

Knight Commander Plaguefist is a high ranking Death Knight of the Scourge. He is seen outside of the Chapel of the Crimson Flame. There the Scourge troops under his command lay waste to the chapel, tossing flaming torches on it at regular intervals. He also guards a number of prisoners from the Argent Dawn, having young Death Knights execute them; however, he mentions they were originally prisoners of the Scarlet Crusade whom the Scourge found by accident rather than capturing themselves. It is unknown if he remained under control of the Lich King or became one of the Knights of the Ebon Blade after the Battle for Light's Hope Chapel.

The kodo or kodo beast (sometimes pluralized as kodos) is a large omnivorous herd animal native to the Barrens. The tauren hold these reptilian creatures in high esteem, and breed them as mounts. They are also used extensively as pack animals by both the goblins and the Horde as a whole. The Blackrock clan are also known to use war kodos.

Kobolds (pronounced "KOH-bawld") are a race of diminutive, rat-like subterranean humanoids who dwell in and around caverns and mines throughout the Eastern Kingdoms, Kalimdor and the Broken Isles. They are not particularly intelligent and are notoriously cowardly, preferring to keep their distance from other, larger races. Kobolds are famous for being obsessively protective of the candles they wear upon their heads and which help them light their way through the dark tunnels they call home. A race of arctic kobolds known as snobolds make their home in the frozen wastes of Northrend.

The Kodo Graveyard is a large gaveyard that is final resting place of the Kodo, location in Desolace. Notably, there is a quest to collect kodo bones that requires adventurers to fight kodo apparitions which materialize when they attempt to loot bones on the ground.

Kor'gall was a ruthless and tyrannical ogre warlord and chieftain of the Stonemaul clan living in Dustwallow Marsh after the Battle for Mount Hyjal. At some point, he came into possession of the ancient orcish axe Serathil.
Kolkar Crag was a craggy gorge in southern Durotar called this way because of the Kolkar centaurs inhabiting it.

Kodo Rock was a natural monument near Camp Narache that tauren shaman needed to go to for one of their early quests. The rock could only be seen from a short distance so one needed to pay attention. To get there, one could travel from Camp Narache directly towards the Brambleblade Ravine and it would be located about halfway along the direct line. A small dirt area would be seen on the minimap to pinpoint it. The Kodo Rock disappeared after the Cataclysm.

The Kolkar clan or tribe is one of five clans of centaur native to Desolace, having settlements in the Barrens and Desolace, and formerly holding Kolkar Crag in southern Durotar. The founding leader (Khan) of the Kolkar was , an alleged son of and and first of the centaur Khans. Later the clan was led by Khan Dez'hepah and his officers, until his death. The clan, or what remains of it, is currently led by Khan Leh'Prah. The Kolkar clan holds no alliance with their brother tribes, and constantly warring with the Horde, Alliance and other centaur alike.

The Kodo Drum Circle is a celebration performed by most tauren tribes once a year. Despite its name, this festival celebrates the sacrifice all animals made to the tauren tribe over the last year. A drum circle, in which a tauren constantly beats a drum until another tauren takes her place, forms and lasts all of a day and a night. The drumming honors the slain animals and asks the blessing of living animals who will give their lives for the tribe in the coming year. It is a bad omen for the drum circle to break before the end of the festival.

The Kor'kron Vanguard is a Horde fortress at the base of Angrathar the Wrathgate, the gate to Icecrown Glacier, in the northern regions of the Dragonblight. The base is made up of a single tower, a burrow and is supplied with catapults and blade throwers.

Kodian is the daughter of Ursoc and niece of Ursol. She can be found at the Heart's Blood Shrine in Grizzly Hills. In fact, she is a prisoner of a sort, as the mad furbolgs of the Redfang tribe won't allow her to leave, and because she loves her people, she would rather stay put than hurt any of them. After the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard managed to slip past the furbolgs to speak with Kodian, who was still present in the shrine to continue her duty. She explained that her brother Orsonn is also still prisoner at Rage Fang Shrine, and that both of them still hope that someday their people will find peace among themselves. The Kodo Run is an event that happens at least once a year. The day is officially declared by the shaman when they have determined the time is right. A group of Tauren hunters search for a herd of Kodo and then set up and hide behind portable grass blinds. They wait until the herd of kodo are near them and then surprise the herd by various means like lighting a bonfire behind them, jumping up and down from behind their blinds, shaking rattlers, and just plain scaring them so that the herd becomes confounded. __NOTOC__ :A mighty Kraken that patrols the dark waters of the Abyssal Depths. Kolorath is a kraken found swimming in a circle around the entire border of the Abyssal Depths. He can be kited, however his melee swings hit for well over 800k damage and drops only a few silver for your efforts. It is somewhat notable that as of Patch 4.0.6, Kolorath cannot be traditionally reset with range like other similar slow-moving Vashj'ir NPCs (such as the Whale Shark). Although a player can get far enough away that they will drop combat, Kolorath will continue to follow them until he is killed, or they cause him to evade. There is no achievement related to defeating Kolorath.
Konu's Platemail is a quest reward from More Than Illness (Horde).
Kodo Steak and Ribs is a food shop found on the High Rise of Thunder Bluff.

Kor'kron Squad Commander is a Kor'kron agent found at the Twilight Gate in the Twilight Highlands during the Horde quest Up to the Citadel.
Konu Runetotem is a tauren quest giver and leader of Camp Ataya in Feralas. He has found signs of a disturbing illness.
Kor'kron Necrolytes are blood elves and Forsaken of Kor'kron located in Icecrown Citadel. They are the Horde equivalent of the Alliance's Skybreaker Summoners.

Kong is a pandaren child seen playing with Jie in the Mandori Village on the Wandering Isle.
Kor'kron Air Marines are orcs seen during the quest: Twilight Skies (2).
__NOTOC__ Kol Ironpaw is a master of the Way of the Grill, a style of Pandaren cooking. He can be found at the Halfhill Market in the Valley of the Four Winds.
Kor'kron Vanquishers are blood elves of Kor'kron located in Icecrown Citadel.
Kobeyaks are yaks located at Kota Basecamp and the Grummle Bazaar in Kun-Lai Summit.

Kor'ik is a Klaxxi quest giver, helping the player awaken the Paragons. During Corruption Runs Deep, he is exposed by Hisek the Swarmkeeper as a double agent working for Grand Empress Shek'zeer, and subsequently killed by Hisek and the player. His place in the Klaxxi'vess is now held by Zer'ik.

The Kor'kron Loyalist was once found on the docks at Bladefist Bay in Durotar, where he would encounter goblin adventurers and send them to Warchief Hellscream. His current whereabouts and status are unknown. He may have been killed during the Darkspear Rebellion as he was replaced by Darkspear Loyalist.
Kor'kron Riding Wolves are wolves located at Wrathgate in the Dragonblight.
Kodiack is a Technical Support MVP on the US forums. He posts as a level 85 male blood elf hunter from Thrall US.

Kor'kron Jo'mag is an orc that can be found on the Hellscream's Fist in the Jade Forest. Along with Dubs, Spisak and Shin, he's one of the Kor'kron Guards that accompanies General Nazgrim to the new uncharted land. When the airship is burning in the Jade Forest, he can be seen talking with Nazgrim. Since this is his only appearance, it can be argued that he never left the airship, and died when it was taken down later.

Kor'kron Spisak is an orc that can be found on the Hellscream's Fist in the Jade Forest. Along with Dubs, Jo'mag and Shin, he's one of the Kor'kron Guards that accompanies General Nazgrim to the new uncharted land. When the airship is burning in the Jade Forest, he can be seen knelt, tending to the heavily wounded Sky Master Corpora. Kofa the Swift is a pandaren bow and crossbow vendor residing in Honeydew Village in the Jade Forest. He stands next to Ethan Graveborn, near the village inn. During the third invasion of the Burning Legion, he was located in the Trueshot Lodge.

Kor'kron Marines are orcs located in Mogujia and Garrosh'ar Advance in Kun-Lai Summit where they guard Garrosh Hellscream and Shan Kien. They also appear during the Assault on Zan'vess.

The Kor'kron Disguise is created by combining a Kor'kron Helmet, a set of Kor'kron Armor, and a pair of Kor'kron Boots, all of which are dropped from Kor'kron at Garrosh'ar Advance in east-central Kun-Lai Summit. It is then provided for the followup quest, Memory Wine (Alliance). Using the disguise turns all Horde units (even Garrosh) at the camp friendly.
Kor'dok and Tinzo the Emberkeeper are mogu located on the Isle of Thunder.
Kor'kron Flameworgs are hell hounds located in Northern Barrens.

Kor'kron Butchers are orcs found at Kor'kron meat camp in the Northern Barrens.
Kor'kron Incinerators are Kor'kron orcs located at the Kor'kron refinery in the Northern Barrens. They are equipped with flamethrowers, and are not hostile to low-level Horde adventurers.
Kor'kron Demolishers are demolishers located in the Kor'kron refinery in Northern Barrens.
Kor'kron Caravan Raiders were orcs located in the Northern Barrens. Riding a Kor'kron Battlewolf, they were attacking the Barrens Caravan.

Kor'kron Commanders have been placed in Northern Barrens to oversee the Kor'kron war effort. Like the Champions of Lei Shen on the Isle of Thunder, the commanders' total health will scale in relation to how many characters are attacking it. Additionally, the commanders are completely shared tap, even across factions. Commanders do not have a set spawn location, but each commander does have a zone-wide yell when it appears. One or two commanders will generally be up at all times, and they are marked by a on the zone map. Commanders are immune to many forms of crowd control, including charm and fear effects.
Kor'kron Spotters are orcs of Kor'kron located at Dranosh'ar Blockade of Durotar.

Kor'kron Stone was used as a currency for the Darkspear Rebellion. It dropped from various high-level mobs in the Northern Barrens, such as Kor'kron Earthshakers, Kor'kron Flameworgs, Kor'kron Immolators, and Wild Earths. It could also be looted from Kor'kron Stone Crates and Surplus Supplies.

Kor'kron Lumber dropped from various high-level NPCs in the Northern Barrens, such as Hellscream Laborers, Kor'kron Marauders, Mercenary Shredders, and Kor'kron Assassins. It could also be looted from Kor'kron Lumber piles, Kor'kron Lumber Crates, and Surplus Supplies.

Kor'kron Warmongers are orcs located in Durotar. They are attacking Sen'jin Village.
